items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: That's where Count Basie became famous for playing that song, 'Jumping at the Woodside.'

ctx.x: Then you go up to Harlem. And what was your first reaction of going up there? What was your feeling about the place? Well, describe what Harlem was like in those days.

Well, Harlem had a place called the Woodside Hotel. And it was very popular. That's where all the elite of Harlem mostly lived there, and in fact that's where Count Basie became famous for playing that song, 'Jumping at the Woodside.'

Well, Mr. Bubbles was very strict too, you know. He was a family man. He was only man in the family there, his -- his wife, his mother and his elder sister, and then he had a younger -- younger sister, Tiny. She lived around the corner from them. That was up at 154th Street.

And…

And at that time, see, I was supposed to be the protege of Mr. Buck. And Chuckles was supposed to be the protege of John Bubbles. But Bubbles had a way of tap dancing, an invention of his, and he had cut the tempo in half. And -- but his dancing consisted of more rhythms, better patterns of tap steps and so on, and I was trying to interest Chuckles in how to tap dance like Mr. Bubbles because I had learnt my part, see.
